facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of a slowly growing, dull, intermittent swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule
fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area
teeth #15 and #16 were grossly carious
a firm, mildly tender diffuse swelling of the adjacent vestibular mucosa
no tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth
a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices
a provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made
preoperative blood tests were within normal limits
curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue
a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma

concepts.why: The patient presented with a slowly growing swelling and discomfort in the right upper vestibule, and a provisional diagnosis of a periapical abscess was made based on the clinical and radiographic findings.
The curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue, which is consistent with a periapical granuloma, and a provisional diagnosis of periapical granuloma was made.
The patient had grossly carious teeth, which is a sign of dental caries.
The patient presented with fluctuations in pain intensity and a sensation of heaviness in the area, which is consistent with chronic periapical periodontitis.
The patient had a mild periapical radiolucency at the affected root apices, which is consistent with acute periapical periodontitis.
The curettage yielded a gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue, which could be consistent with a periapical cyst.

frontier_selector.rationale: The gelatinous, soft, mushy tissue obtained from curettage and the absence of tenderness on percussion of the involved teeth support the diagnosis of periapical granuloma over periapical abscess.
